questions.q: Why must the approval checkpoint sit before a sensitive tool executes rather than after?
options: It doesn't matter when it happens, as long as it happens eventually
Once a tool like issue_refund runs, the action is done -- reviewing it afterward can't undo it, making approval meaningless
The Messages API only allows checkpoints after execution
Approving before execution is slower than approving after
questions.explain: For an irreversible action, review only matters if it happens before the action runs. Reviewing after execution can't undo what already happened.

questions.q: What happens if your code simply drops a rejected tool call instead of sending any tool_result for it?
options: Nothing -- the Messages API treats a missing result the same as an approval
The conversation can't continue correctly; the API expects a tool_result for every tool_use block it sent
Claude automatically assumes the action was approved
The rejected tool executes anyway as a fallback
questions.explain: The Messages API requires a tool_result for every tool_use before the conversation proceeds -- skipping one breaks the expected format, which is why a rejection still has to be sent as a real (is_error: true) result.

questions.q: What does setting is_error: true on a rejected tool_result actually do?
options: It deletes the pending approval record
It marks the result as a failure/denial Claude should react to and incorporate into its next response, rather than treating it as normal data
It automatically retries the tool call
It has no functional effect, it's purely cosmetic
questions.explain: is_error signals to Claude that the tool call didn't succeed as requested, so Claude incorporates the reason into its response instead of treating the content as a normal successful result.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend an instructive rejection message (what was wrong, what to try next) instead of a bare 'denied' string?
options: Bare strings are not valid JSON
An instructive message gives Claude real information to act on, the same principle as writing a good tool-execution error message
The Messages API requires rejection messages to be at least 50 characters
It has no effect on Claude's behavior either way
questions.explain: Just like a tool execution error, a specific, instructive rejection message lets Claude adapt and respond usefully instead of just reporting a vague failure.

questions.q: What Messages API formatting rule most directly shapes how 'waiting for a human' has to be implemented?
options: Tool definitions must be sorted alphabetically by name
tool_result blocks must immediately follow their tool_use message, with no other messages in between -- so the wait has to happen in your own application state, not mid-API-call
Only one tool can be defined per request
System prompts cannot exceed 1000 characters
questions.explain: Because tool_result must immediately follow tool_use with nothing in between, the pending approval has to be held in your own application/database state, with the next Messages API request only sent once a decision is made.
